_help: Edit the four model names, then run: node tools/set-models.mjs. Planning agents (strongest) decide quality — give them your best model. The reviewer must be a DIFFERENT model (ideally another family) from the coder's, or it shares the coder's blind spots; set-models warns if not.
_note: BUDGET profile (22 Oct, after a real run: planning one login screen cost ~55% of a 1,290-unit budget, 3 Opus agents ~270 of it). No Opus anywhere; Sonnet 5 only for the five agents whose mistakes spread (wireframe-analyzer, library-advisor, fsd-planner, architect, debugger); Haiku 5.5 for everything else — GitHub describes it as built for subagents and as matching Sonnet 5 on many coding tasks with fewer tokens and steps. Reviewer = a different family, run once per batch. Spend more where results disappoint: set strongest to 'Claude Opus 5 (copilot)' and run set-models.
